topics.label: Course introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the lecture series, and defines the learning objectives regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer development.

topics.label: Fundamental concepts and causes of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the genetic and microenvironmental nature of cancer while examining the relative contributions of stochastic mutations, environmental exposures, and geographical patterns.

topics.label: Pathogens and infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents, specifically highlighting Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma, contribute to malignant transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how dietary toxins, UV radiation, and metabolized chemical carcinogens cause direct and indirect DNA mutations and adducts.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and multistage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters and chronic inflammation cooperate with mutational initiators to drive tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Host developmental stage and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how proliferative developmental windows and hormonal changes influence tissue vulnerability to carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and assessing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro testing methods used to establish carcinogenicity and evaluate exposure risks.
